parole.significato: Vulture.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans aasvogel (“vulture”) (obsolete form of aasvoël), from Dutch aasvogel, from aas (“carrion”) + vogel (“bird”).

parole.significato: A person from South Africa or Namibia who speaks Afrikaans. (More properly called "Afrikaans people" or Afrikaners.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans Afrikaans (“African”) itself from earlier Dutch Afrikaansch (“African”).

parole.significato: Expressing annoyance, remorse, surprise, etc.: oh, ah.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans ag, from Dutch ach.

parole.significato: The policy of racial segregation in South Africa from 1948 to 1994.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans apartheid (literally “separateness, apartness”) (1929 in a South African socio-political context), from Afrikaans apart (“separate”) + suffix -heid, cognate of English -hood.

parole.significato: A hot dry wind blowing from the mountainous interior to the coast.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans bergwind (“mountain wind”), from Dutch bergwind, equivalent to berg + wind.

parole.significato: Any of several species of pufferfish found in South African waters.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans blaasop (“blowfish”), ultimately from Dutch blaas op (“blow up”).

parole.significato: A South African antelope of genus Damaliscus
parole.testo: From Afrikaans bontebok, from Dutch bontebok (literally “motley goat”).

parole.significato: A highly venomous snake found in sub-Saharan Africa, Dispholidus typus.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans boomslang, from Dutch boomslang, composed of boom (“tree”) + slang (“snake”).

parole.significato: A barbecue (grill), especially an open outdoor grill built specifically for the purpose of braaing.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans braai (“to grill”), from Dutch braden (“roast”).

parole.significato: Short pants; shorts.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans broekie, diminutive of broek (“pants”), from Dutch broek (“pants”). Cognate with Dutch broekje (“shorts”). Doublet of breeches and britches.

parole.significato: A ridge or small hill.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans bult, that from Dutch bult.

parole.significato: Thanks.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans dankie, from Dutch dank je.

parole.significato: A small, herbivorous mammal in the order Hyracoidea, the rock hyrax.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans dassie, from Dutch das (“badger”).

parole.significato: One of the poles supporting a wagon.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans disselboom, from Dutch disselboom, a compound of dissel (“support pole”) and boom (“tree; beam”).

parole.significato: A cloth.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans doek (“cloth”), from Dutch doek, from Middle Dutch doec, from Old Dutch *duok, from Proto-West Germanic *dōk, from Proto-Germanic *dōkaz. Doublet of duck.

parole.significato: To beat up; clobber; thrash.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans donder (“thrash”), from Dutch donder (“thunder”). Doublet of thunder.

parole.significato: vagina
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans doos, from Dutch doos. Doublet of dose.

parole.significato: Any of several species of small southern African antelopes of the Cephalophinae subfamily.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans duiker (literally “diver”), from Dutch duiker, from Middle Dutch dukere. Piecewise doublet of ducker.

parole.significato: A genus of large South African antelope (Taurotragus), valued both for its hide and flesh.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans eland, from Dutch eland (“elk”), from Middle Dutch elant, from obsolete early modern German elend, from Middle High German elen, see German Elen for more. Doublet of elk.

parole.significato: A traditional Afrikaner dish of baked (or sometimes deep-fried) meatballs prepared with onion, bread, eggs, vinegar, an…
parole.testo: From Afrikaans frikkadel, from Dutch frikadel. Doublet of fricandeau and frikadelle.

parole.significato: A large African antelope (Oryx gazella).
parole.testo: From Afrikaans gemsbok, from Dutch gemsbok, from gems (“chamois”) + bok (“buck”), the former from German Gämse, of uncertain origin.

parole.significato: A small antelope of genus Raphicerus from South Africa.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans grysbok, from Dutch grijsbok, from grijs (“gray”) + bok (“buck, billy goat”).

parole.significato: A kind of large mound, of disputed origin, above or near the surface of the landscape in parts of South Africa.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans, from Dutch heuveltje (“hillock”).

parole.significato: A kind of small hut.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans hok, from Dutch hok.

parole.significato: Yes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans ja (“yes”), from Dutch ja (“yes”). More at yea.

parole.significato: A friendly term of address, especially for a young man.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans jong (“male servant; boy”), from Dutch jongen (“young”).

parole.significato: A type of fish from southern Africa, Argyrosomus coronus.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans kabeljou, from Dutch kabeljauw (“cod”).

parole.significato: Trouble.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans kak (“shit”), from Dutch kak (“shit”). See also cack.

parole.significato: A popular South African food fish; Genypterus capensis.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans kingklip (“king rock fish”), from Dutch koningklipvisch.

parole.significato: A small antelope native to eastern and southern Africa having a dense, brown, speckled coat (Oreotragus oreotragus).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans klipspringer, from Dutch klipspringer, both literally meaning "rock-jumper".

parole.significato: Any of several large game fish of the family Sciaenidae, especially the kabeljou (dusky kob or great kob or perhaps the…
parole.testo: From Afrikaans kob, from Dutch kobbe (“fish, goby, lumpfish”).

parole.significato: A traditional Afrikaner confection consisting of a deep-fried twisted or plaited doughnut dipped in syrup immediately a…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans koeksister, from Dutch koek + sissen.

parole.significato: A hill or mountain.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans kop, from Dutch kop, from Middle Dutch cop.

parole.significato: An encircling or overhanging wall of rock.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans krans, from Dutch krans, from Middle Dutch crans, from Middle High German kranz, from Old High German kranz, probably altered from krenz, ultimately related to Proto-Germanic *kringaz (“circle, ring”). The English spelling seems to have been influenced by cognate German Kranz

parole.significato: bad-tempered, aggressive, fierce
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans kwaai, attributive form of kwaad, from Dutch kwaad.

parole.significato: loincloth
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans lappie, from Dutch lappie, Hollandic form of lapje (“a little rag”).

parole.significato: Tasty, nice, fun, great.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans lekker, from Dutch lekker.

parole.significato: An ear or kernel of maize; in plural as mass noun: maize, corn.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans mielie, from obsolete Dutch milie (“millet, maize”), from Old French mil (“millet”).

parole.significato: Suricata suricatta, a small carnivorous mammal of the mongoose family, from the Kalahari Desert, known for its habit of…
parole.testo: From Afrikaans meerkat, transferred use of Dutch meerkat (“guenon [monkey]”), from Middle Dutch meercatte (literally “sea cat”), compare English mercat. Sometimes suggested to be influenced by or derived from an Indian source; compare Hindi मर्कट (markaṭ, “ape, monkey”) and Sanskrit मर्कट (markaṭa).

parole.significato: A ridge between ruts made by wheels in a dirt or gravel road.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans middelmannetjie (“little man in the middle”) (analysable as middel (“middle”) + man (“man”) + -etjie (“diminutive suffix”)), from Dutch middel (“middle”) + mannetje (“a short man”) (from man (“man”) + -etje, a variant of -tje (diminutive suffix)).

parole.significato: Any of various species of sparrow, especially Passer melanurus.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans, from Dutch mus (“a sparrow”).

parole.significato: mosquito, gnat
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans muggie, diminutive of mug, from Dutch mug, from Middle Dutch mugge.

parole.significato: A species of weasel found in southern Africa, Poecilogale albinucha.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans muishond, from Dutch muishond, from Middle Dutch muushont.

parole.significato: A tax on produce, stock, and capitation.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans opgaaf, from Dutch opgaaf, variant of opgave.

parole.significato: A fellow, guy, bloke.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans ou, probably from Dutch ouwe (“old man”).

parole.significato: abalone
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans perlemoen, from Dutch perlemoer (“mother-of-pearl”).

parole.significato: The country, the countryside.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans platteland, from Dutch platteland.

parole.significato: The female genitalia.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans poes (“vagina”), from Dutch poes (“cat, female cat, vagina”). Doublet of puss.

parole.significato: To jump with all four limbs at once.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans pronk (“to show off, strut, or prance”), from Dutch pronken (“to show off, be flamboyant”). See also prank.

parole.significato: Any viper or adder in genus Bitis,
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans or South African Dutch pofadder.

parole.significato: A rocky slope, especially the area over a river valley; specifically, the Rand
parole.testo: Named after Witwatersrand; the last element is Afrikaans rand (“ridge”), from Dutch rand, from Old Saxon rand, from Germanic *randaz. Compare Etymology 1, and Rand. The sense of currency is because of gold that was extracted from the Witwatersrand rocks.

parole.significato: A medium-sized, deerlike South African antelope, Pelea capreolus, having pale-gray, curly fur and straight horns.
parole.testo: Earlier rabock, reebok, rhebuck, rheeboc, raybuck, rehboc, borrowed from Afrikaans reebok (“rhebok”), ribbok (“rhebok”), from Dutch reebok (“roebuck”), compound of ree + bok, from Middle Dutch reeboc. Unetymological h present since 1775 though the spelling and pronunciation has varied greatly over t

parole.significato: Any member of the species Procavia capensis of mammals with a rodent-like appearance, but not closely related to rodent…
parole.testo: From rock + badger. From Afrikaans dassie, from Dutch das (“badger”).

parole.significato: A shrub (Aspalathus linearis) from which a tisane (herbal tea) is made.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Afrikaans rooibos (literally “redbush”), from Dutch rooi (“red”) + bos (“bush”). Compare related honeybush via Afrikaans heuningbos from heuning (“honey”) + bos (“bush”).

parole.significato: A stout whip, especially made of rhinoceros or hippopotamus hide.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans sjambok, from Dutch sjambok, from Javanese cambuk, and as borrowed in Malay: modern Indonesian and Malay, ultimately from Persian چابک (čâbok). Originally spelt in the colonial Dutch transliteration tscamboek. The term was imported by VOC officials, Dutch merchants, the Maardijkers (M

parole.significato: A hoodlum, a petty criminal.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans skollie, from Dutch schoelje, from Middle Dutch schoelie.

parole.significato: A cigarette.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans skyf (“a slice; disk”), from Dutch schijf, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *skībǭ. Doublet of shive and skive.

parole.significato: A scam or deception; fast one.
parole.testo: Originally South African slang, borrowed from Afrikaans slenter (“scam”) from Dutch schlenter (“trick”)

parole.significato: A ditch.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans sloot, from Dutch sloot, from Middle Dutch slote, sloot, from Old Dutch *slōt, from Proto-West Germanic *slaut.

parole.significato: A peddler.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans smous or Dutch smous, from a Yiddish word whose precise origin is uncertain. One theory is that it derives from Yiddish משה (moyshe, “Moses”), pronounced moushe in Western Yiddish, from Hebrew מֹשֶׁה (moshé, “Moses”).

parole.significato: An edible fish, Thyrsites atun, native to South African (Cape), South American and Australian waters, often smoked or s…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans snoek, from Dutch snoek, from Middle Dutch snoec, from Old Dutch *snuoc. Some senses come from or are influenced by Dutch zeesnoek (“barracuda”, literally “sea pike”), a word that Van Riebeeck applied to the Thyrsites atun. Doublet of snook and possibly a distant doublet of s

parole.significato: The track, trail, droppings, or scent of an animal.
parole.testo: Early 19th century, from Afrikaans spoor, from Dutch spoor (“track”). Akin to Old English and Old Norse spor (whence Danish spor), and German Spur, all from Proto-Germanic *spurą. Compare spurn.

parole.significato: A small, fast antelope native to southern Africa, Antidorcas marsupialis.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans springbok, from Dutch springbok, from springen (“to jump, spring”) + bok (“buck, billy goat, antelope”).

parole.significato: town, village
parole.testo: From Afrikaans and Dutch stad (“city, town”), from Middle Dutch stat, from Old Dutch stad, from Proto-Germanic *stadiz (“place”), from Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂tis (“standing, position”). Doublet of stead.

parole.significato: A common small antelope of southern and eastern Africa, Raphicerus campestris.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans steenbok, from Dutch steenbok.

parole.significato: The shallow-water Cape hake (Merluccius capensis)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans stokvis, from Dutch stokvis.

parole.significato: A raised veranda in front of a house.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans stoep, from Dutch stoep, from Middle Dutch stoep. Doublet of stoop.

parole.significato: beachcomber
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans strandloper, from Dutch strandloper.

parole.significato: To make up, to fabricate, to pull out of one's ass.
parole.testo: Calque of Afrikaans uit sy duim suig, from Dutch uit zijn duim zuigen.

parole.significato: An older female authority figure.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans tannie (“auntie”), diminutive of tante (“aunt”), from Dutch tante (“aunt”).

parole.significato: A rapprochement.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans toenadering, from Dutch toenadering.

parole.significato: A journey by ox wagon.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans trek, from Dutch trekken, from Middle Dutch trekken (weak verb) and trēken (“to trek, place, bring, move”, strong verb), from Old Dutch *trekkan, *trekan, from Proto-West Germanic *trekan, from Proto-Germanic *trekaną, *trakjaną (“to drag, haul, scrape, pull”), from Proto-Indo-Europea

parole.significato: A prison.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans tronk, from Dutch tronk, from Portuguese tronco, from Latin truncus. Doublet of truncus and trunk.

parole.significato: The edible bulb of certain plants.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans uintjie, from Dutch ajuintje (“little onion”).

parole.significato: A foreigner; outlander.
parole.testo: Attested since 1890. From Afrikaans uitlander (“foreigner”), from Dutch uitlander (“foreigner”). Cognate and confluenced with outlander.

parole.significato: Very raw young wine, usually with sediment.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans [Term?], from Dutch vaal (“pale, cloudy”) + japie (“Jack or Jim”).

parole.significato: politically optimistic and receptive to change
parole.testo: From Afrikaans verlig from Dutch verlicht.

parole.significato: A shallow wetland or minor lake, generally a seasonal one, or the lowland where such a wetland appears seasonally.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans vlei, from Dutch vallei (“valley”). Doublet of valley and vly.

parole.significato: The crawling form of a locust, not yet able to fly.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans voetganger, from Dutch voetganger, from Middle Dutch voetganger.

parole.significato: Any plant of the subfamily Mesembryanthemoideae, succulent groundcovers.
parole.testo: From Afrikaans diminutive of vy(g) (“fig”), from Dutch vijg (“fig”).

parole.significato: boerewors
parole.testo: From Afrikaans wors, from Dutch worst (“sausage”). Doublet of wurst.

parole.significato: Synonym of sitting room.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Afrikaans sitkamer, from Dutch zitkamer.
